title: Deep queue thaw and rollback safety sprint kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share rollback playbook draft and annotated runbook link: https://app.redwood/repo/rollback-playbook
Customer to provide last 48h request traces and hotspot dashboard links
Redwood SE to run token-level cost/latency breakdown for queued workloads by EOD 2026-11-27

Raj Patel - Share 48h traces + hotspot Grafana link - 2026-11-26

summary: Postmortem follow-up focused on the long queue accumulation event during peak inference (2026-11-21). Call covered root-cause hypothesis (autoscaler backoff + KV cache eviction interplay), immediate mitigations, and a safety-first rollout plan (controlled rollback + automation gates). Agreement on an action sprint: produce an automated rollback playbook, share detailed traces, rehearse runbook, and validate telemetry thresholds for early detection.
header:
Date: 2026-11-25 | Time: 15:00 PST | Duration: 60m
Attendees: Sarah Lin (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Imani Brooks (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Northbridge VP Eng), Raj Patel (Northbridge SRE), Olivia Greene (Northbridge Security), Tom Barlow (Platform Eng)
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio OK?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Yep, loud and clear. Sorry, we had a few folks in back to back but we cleared the room.
[00:15] Sarah Lin: Cool. The goal today is to align on the incident root cause, confirm the mitigations Diego proposed, and kick off a short sprint to get an automated rollback + runbook in place. We'll also want to agree on rehearsal timing.
[00:28] Diego Ruiz: Quick recap — on 11/21 you saw sustained queue depth rise that didn't self-heal because the autoscaler hit a backoff loop while several nodes were in warmup; simultaneously the KV cache eviction led to repeated full attention recompute which spiked token time. So cost + latency amplified and requests backed up.
[00:48] Raj Patel: Yeah that's our read. The weird part — sometimes the nodes were healthy but didn't accept traffic; could be scheduling or the consumer group mark. We saw a spike at 03:14 UTC and then the thrash.
[01:10] Tom Barlow: Also, we had a rolling deploy that day — small config tweak to batching. Not sure if that induced a short window of cold starts.
[01:25] Diego Ruiz: Right, the batch setting change increased per-request buffer window which interacts poorly with continuous batching heuristics. Our runtime's prefetch threshold and the new batch window conspired to push more tokens into the pipeline before a flush. In practice that's harmless at low load but at 10k rps it amplified.
[01:50] Maya Chen: Can you explain the KV cache eviction tie again? We track cache hit rate but not eviction patterns.
[01:55] Diego Ruiz: Sure. When the sequence length distribution jumps, KV memory pressure goes up. Our eviction policy is LRU-ish but with a soft TTL; when memory crosses threshold it aggressively evicts prefixes, which forces model to recompute large KV blocks at next request, increasing latency per token.
[02:20] Olivia Greene: Are those eviction decisions logged centrally? For audit we need to be able to reconstruct who did what for data residency and to prove we didn't leak embeddings.
[02:30] Imani Brooks: We flagged that as a telemetry gap. Diego, can you confirm what exists today?
[02:35] Diego Ruiz: Right now we emit eviction events but they're high-cardinality and not currently forwarded to the long-term audit store unless the trace is sampled. We can change that but it has cost implications — storage and query.
[02:50] Raj Patel: For us, the ask is to have a windowed dump or indexed pointer so we can replay the last 1h during incidents.
[02:57] Diego Ruiz: Makes sense. We'll propose a compact eviction trace format that points to the node/time/keyspace rather than full payloads.
[03:10] Sarah Lin: Good. Let's move to mitigations — Diego, you had an immediate mitigation to limit batch window and add a throttle guard for queue length, right?
[03:19] Diego Ruiz: Yes. Short term: revert the batching param to the previous value, cap per-node in-flight tokens, and add a queue-depth circuit that kicks in before autoscaler backoff. Medium term: smarter warmup and prefer burstable nodes during deployments.
[03:35] Maya Chen: What's the rollback path you'd recommend if something similar happens in prod during a peak? Our ops team wants a safe, automated playbook.
[03:45] Diego Ruiz: We recommend a staged rollback with automated canary checks: 1) pause new deployments, 2) scale up a warm pool of nodes, 3) toggle batching param via feature flag, 4) progressively reroute traffic off the problematic revision, 5) abort if error rate or latency crosses threshold.
[04:02] Raj Patel: We need the exact SLO gates — what thresholds?
[04:06] Diego Ruiz: Preliminary: token p95 > 600ms for 2 continuous minutes OR queue depth > 80% of target capacity for 3 minutes triggers the rollback stage. We can tune after rehearsal.
[04:25] Olivia Greene: From security we also need the rollback to be logged with KMS key IDs for any secrets used during the rollback, and the audit entry should include the operator and a signed timestamp.
[04:40] Sarah Lin: That's covered in Redwood Private patterns but for hosted we can integrate with your KMS. We'll note the exact audit fields in the playbook doc.
[04:50] Maya Chen: One other constraint — we rotate keys nightly for a small subset of workloads. If the rollback requires re-seeding or re-authorization we could be blocked.
[04:59] Olivia Greene: Yeah confirm that any ephemeral credentialing step in the playbook doesn't depend on an out-of-band key that might be rotated.
[05:07] Diego Ruiz: Good catch. We'll add safe-gates: check KMS key active window and fail open to manual approval if rotated keys are present.
[05:16] Imani Brooks: I'll capture that as an explicit action item.
[05:20] Sarah Lin: Let's talk telemetry and detection. Raj, what do you already have?
[05:26] Raj Patel: We have per-route latency, queue length, token rates, and host health. Missing: eviction traces, per-token decode time, and a clear signal for warmup completion. Our alerting is noisy atm.
[05:40] Diego Ruiz: On Redwood side we can ship a small agent that reports warmup complete events and a compact eviction pointer. Also propose a composite alert in Grafana that looks at combined signals to reduce noise.
[05:53] Tom Barlow: How invasive is the agent? We need it to run under our CI and pass security review.
[05:59] Diego Ruiz: It's minimal — reads local runtime metrics and posts to an authenticated webhook. No payloads beyond metadata. We can show the code in the repo.
[06:10] Olivia Greene: We'll want an initial security review before we run it. Please prep an SBOM and 3rd-party deps list.
[06:18] Sarah Lin: Noted. Diego, can you produce the agent repo link plus SBOM by Friday?
[06:22] Diego Ruiz: Yes.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Okay, stepping back — what's the plan for rehearsing this? We don't want first time to be in a live emergency.
[06:31] Imani Brooks: Proposed: a 2-hour rehearsal next week with a controlled load spike in staging and simulated KV eviction; run the rollback playbook and measure time to recovery.
[06:42] Raj Patel: 2 hours seems tight; recommend 3 hours to allow pre-checks, dry run, and postmortem.
[06:47] Sarah Lin: Let's tentatively book 2.5 hours, but we'll be flexible. Action: Imani will send options for 12/1–12/3.
[06:56] Diego Ruiz: For the playbook format, I'll provide both a human-readable runbook and a machine-actionable YAML that can be executed by our orchestration. The YAML will have gates and abort conditions.
[07:09] Tom Barlow: Machine-actionable is ideal but security will want manual approval gates.
[07:14] Olivia Greene: We require a two-person approval for any automated rollback that manipulates KMS or deletes keys. For other parameters a single operator is OK.
[07:24] Diego Ruiz: We'll add two-step auth for KMS-affecting steps.
[07:27] Maya Chen: Let's also document which routes are critical and which can be deprioritized during rollback.
[07:33] Raj Patel: I'll share our route priority list and SLO mappings.
[07:36] Sarah Lin: Great — now some quick commercial notes: you asked about Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput; we can provision a warm pool as part of the Dedicated offering which removes scheduling cold-starts. Imani can follow-up.
[07:50] Imani Brooks: We'll include cost estimate vs. risk tradeoff in the follow-up doc.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Heads-up: procurement expects a small addendum to the contract around rollback SLAs. We'll involve procurement once we have the playbook.
[08:03] Sarah Lin: Understood. We'll flag that.
[08:06] Diego Ruiz: One more technical note — the KV cache TTL tuning is a low-friction change. We propose moving from soft TTL to percentile-based retention for high fan-out endpoints. That should reduce mass-evictions during load spikes.
[08:23] Raj Patel: Sounds good, but will that increase memory footprint long term?
[08:27] Diego Ruiz: Slightly, but we can enforce a per-customer memory cap and evict based on recent access patterns; tradeoff is better latency stability.
[08:39] Maya Chen: Ok. If we do this we want a canary and metrics to show reduced eviction rate.
[08:46] Sarah Lin: We'll add that to the playbook: canary rollout and metric checklist.
[08:51] Olivia Greene: Also, include a compliance checklist: which logs are stored, retention windows, and redaction rules.
[08:57] Diego Ruiz: Yep, will include that.
[09:00] Imani Brooks: Quick recap and owners: Diego will draft playbook + agent repo + SBOM; Raj provides traces and route priority; Sarah sends commercial and pilot terms; Olivia confirms KMS constraints; Imani sets rehearsal date.
[09:16] Maya Chen: That captures it. Anything else?
[09:19] Tom Barlow: One small ask — can we get a risk heatmap showing probability vs impact for each mitigations? Helps procurement.
[09:25] Sarah Lin: We'll add a simple heatmap slide to the follow-up packet.
[09:29] Diego Ruiz: I'll also include sample thresholds and an initial YAML for the rollback automation.
[09:33] Sarah Lin: Alright thanks everyone. We'll send the notes and the first draft playbook by Friday. Meeting adjourned.
[09:40] End of recording.
